name: Beige Red
lede: Beige Red is a dusty terracotta from the RAL system, named for its warmer, redder place in the beige family.

sections.title: A RAL warm beige
sections.body: Our library dates Beige Red to the RAL system, color 3012, from 1927; the hex here is an approximate screen value rather than a measured swatch [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[onion-skin-pink]], [[antique-brass]], [[copper-crayola]] and [[clay]], at 3.5, 3.9, 4 and 4.1 ΔE [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 classes a close match as a dark yellowish pink [1]. 5, 3.9, 4 and 4.1 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Beige Red in 452 of 23,781 paintings (1.9 percent), as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1500s, in 47 of 2,231 paintings, at 2.2 times the archive's overall rate for that century, and is over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.3 times the expected rate [2]. Maurice Denis used it most relative to his own museums' baseline [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, and the earliest dated match, from 1230, long predates the 1927 RAL record, which only means a similar hue was photographed there, not that the name or the dye existed yet, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
